title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
abstract: Introduces a classifier that estimates question complexity and dynamically routes queries among no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval strategies, targeting a better effectiveness-efficiency tradeoff.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Treats evidence sufficiency as a set-level property rather than independent passage relevance. It aggregates coverage, relation strength, disagreement, conflict, and retrieval uncertainty into support, refute, or insufficient decisions and supports selective answering with calibrated risk.

title: Stop-RAG: Value-Based Retrieval Control for Iterative RAG
abstract: Models iterative RAG as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and learns a value-based controller that chooses whether further retrieval is useful or the system should stop. It directly compares adaptive stopping with fixed-iteration and prompting-based stopping baselines.

title: When Should Active RAG Retrieve? A Budget-Aware Evaluation of Utility, Calibration, and Cost
abstract: Recasts active retrieval as utility estimation and evaluates retrieval triggers under explicit budgets, calibration transfer, retrieval harm, and cost. The study shows that nominal thresholds and router rankings can fail to transfer reliably across datasets and budgets.

title: TASR: Training-Free Adaptive Stopping for Iterative Retrieval
abstract: Proposes a training-free stopping rule for iterative retrieval that combines normalized answer stability with an isotonically calibrated logit-margin signal. The rule is evaluated across multiple models, retrievers, corpora, and dense-retrieval settings with calibration held fixed across extensions.

title: When Iterative RAG Beats Ideal Evidence: A Diagnostic Study in Scientific Multi-hop Question Answering
abstract: Compares no-context, oracle-context, and iterative-RAG conditions for scientific multi-hop QA and diagnoses retrieval coverage, query quality, compositional reasoning, and control calibration. It identifies early-stopping miscalibration and late-hop retrieval failures as continuing controller weaknesses.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Trains a language model to retrieve on demand and emit reflection signals about retrieval relevance, factual support, and generation quality. Retrieval can therefore be skipped or invoked repeatedly rather than being a fixed one-shot operation.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces a retrieval evaluator that estimates the quality of retrieved evidence and triggers different corrective actions when evidence is weak. The framework can extend retrieval with web search and decomposes and recomposes retrieved information before generation.

title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
abstract: Explicitly represents document evolution with version sequences, content boundaries, and changes, and provides intent-routed retrieval for version filtering and change tracking. It also introduces a benchmark for question answering over evolving document versions.

title: MRAG: A Modular Retrieval Framework for Time-Sensitive Question Answering
abstract: Introduces a temporal RAG evaluation setting and a modular framework that separates semantic content from temporal constraints. Retrieval and ranking combine semantic and temporal relevance to improve answering of time-sensitive questions.

title: It's High Time: A Survey of Temporal Information Retrieval and Question Answering
abstract: Surveys temporal information retrieval and question answering, including temporal intent, time expressions, evolving facts, temporal robustness, retrieval-augmented methods, benchmarks, and temporal generalization.

title: Best of Both Worlds: Towards Improving Temporal Knowledge Base Question Answering via Targeted Fact Extraction
abstract: Addresses temporal question answering when a knowledge base lacks the facts required to answer a query. It uses targeted temporal fact extraction to supplement the knowledge base when retrieval alone cannot supply the needed evidence.

title: TempQA: An LLM-based framework for temporal knowledge graph question answering
abstract: Presents a zero-shot temporal knowledge-graph QA framework that converts temporal graph facts into text, retrieves semantically relevant temporal facts, and uses an LLM to reason over them.

title: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift
abstract: Studies abstention for question answering under mixtures of in-domain and out-of-domain examples. It shows that ordinary model confidence can be unreliable under shift and trains a calibrator to predict when answering is sufficiently reliable.

title: Challenges in Information-Seeking QA: Unanswerable Questions and Paragraph Retrieval
abstract: Analyzes unanswerable information-seeking questions and distinguishes failures caused by paragraph retrieval from failures of answerability prediction. The analysis includes retrieval misses and questions requiring evidence distributed across multiple sources.

title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
abstract: Extends conformal prediction beyond ordinary exchangeability to covariate-shift settings using importance weighting based on train-test density ratios. It supplies a foundation for calibrated risk treatment when deployment distributions differ from calibration data.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Constructs selective classifiers around trained neural networks so that predictions can be rejected to meet a target risk level with high probability. It empirically studies the resulting risk-coverage tradeoff.

title: Learn then Test: Calibrating Predictive Algorithms to Achieve Risk Control
abstract: Presents a generic calibration framework that combines learning with multiple-hypothesis testing to select predictive procedures satisfying finite-sample risk requirements without retraining the underlying predictor.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Generalizes conformal methods to control the expected value of monotone loss functions and discusses extensions involving distribution shift and several forms of risk control. It provides a statistical foundation for bounded-risk selective decisions.

title: Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets
abstract: Develops risk-controlling prediction sets with anytime-valid guarantees under sequential and adaptive data collection. It also considers active labeling under a fixed resource budget, making it relevant to controllers that gather evidence adaptively.

title: Distribution-Free, Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets
abstract: Provides distribution-free procedures that calibrate set-valued predictions so their expected loss on future examples is controlled at a user-specified level using held-out calibration data. The work establishes a general finite-sample risk-control framework for black-box predictors.

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
abstract: Derives an optimal rejection rule for statistical recognition and characterizes the tradeoff between recognition error and rejection. It is a foundational formulation of selective decision making with an explicit reject option.

title: A Taxonomy of Time in Databases
abstract: Develops a taxonomy for representing time in database systems and distinguishes multiple temporal dimensions needed to describe changing information. This work is foundational for separating when facts are valid from when they are stored or recorded.

title: A Consensus Glossary of Temporal Database Concepts
abstract: Establishes consensus definitions for temporal-database concepts, including valid time and transaction time. These definitions provide the semantic basis for bitemporal reasoning and distinguishing effective-time validity from database history.

title: Semantics of time-varying information
abstract: Develops systematic semantics for time-varying database information, including valid-time, transaction-time, and bitemporal relations. It provides formal foundations for querying data according to both real-world validity and database-record history.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Formalizes provenance for database query results and distinguishes why-provenance, concerning which source data caused a result, from where-provenance, concerning the source locations from which result values originate.

title: Access control for large collections
abstract: Presents access-control mechanisms designed for large heterogeneous digital collections, addressing scalable authorization structures for subjects, roles, and protected information objects.

title: HONEYBEE: Efficient Role-based Access Control for Vector Databases via Dynamic Partitioning
abstract: Studies nearest-neighbor retrieval when candidate vectors are subject to role-based permission predicates. It introduces dynamic partitioning intended to enforce authorization while controlling the memory and latency costs of permission-constrained vector search.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data

title: ARBITER: AI-Driven Filtering for Role-Based Access Control
abstract: Proposes a RAG security architecture with role-aware retrieval, layered input and output validation, and post-generation checking intended to prevent unauthorized information disclosure under role-based access control.

title: SecureRAG: End-to-End Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Separates retrieval into secure search and secure document fetching, using fully homomorphic encryption for encrypted vector search and attribute-based encryption for fine-grained document access. The system supports dynamic database updates and adaptive access policies.

title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
abstract: Surveys security risks across the RAG knowledge-access pipeline, organizing attacks and defenses by stages and trust boundaries. It covers retrieval-time manipulation and information-exfiltration risks and observes that existing defenses remain fragmented.

title: Provably Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Proposes an encrypted RAG architecture designed to protect both source content and embeddings while limiting retrieval to authorized entities. The work gives formal confidentiality and integrity arguments together with experimental evaluation.

title: Privacy-provisioned-permission-aware RAG in cloud using identity and access management, trust and large-language models (PPPARITL)
abstract: Integrates identity and access management, role-resource-action-condition authorization, trust scoring, and permission-aware retrieval for enterprise RAG. Candidate material is authorized before similarity ranking, and the architecture also protects embeddings and supports revocation of malicious users.

title: CLEAR: Cross-Source Evidence Adjudication for Large Language Models in Medicine
abstract: Combines parametric knowledge, curated local sources, and dynamically retrieved evidence, then jointly assesses candidate answers, supporting evidence, provenance, source quality, agreement, and conflict. Unresolved conflicts trigger targeted follow-up search and another adjudication round, making the framework relevant to explicit failure-driven evidence acquisition.

title: Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Preventing Data Leakage with Provenance and Policy Enforcement
abstract: Presents a RAG governance architecture combining identity-aware filtering, attribute-based access control, policy enforcement, provenance tracking, and auditable refusal behavior. Its evaluation considers leakage, entitlement violations, provenance fidelity, and refusal correctness.
